extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans of comedy, and researchers seeking a biography of Dane Cook
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style biographical profile of a single stand-up comedian (Dane Cook) covering career, style, reception, controversies, and commercial milestones. Used to understand attributes, metrics, and criticisms relevant to a comedian's public and professional evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic style — observational, often vulgar, sometimes dark
rubrics_metrics.description: He is known for his use of observational, often vulgar, and sometimes dark comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the article as a high-level descriptor of the type of material Cook performs; contextual examples include album releases (Harmful If Swallowed, Retaliation, Vicious Circle, Rough Around the Edges, Isolated Incident) and references to his subject matter (human behavior, human sexuality, American politics, gender differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form storytelling and multipurpose phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Cook's style is principally 'long-form storytelling' and 'multipurpose phrases'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explains this as a defining stylistic approach that enables extended anecdotes and recurring lines/phrases that serve multiple punchline functions; this stylistic label is tied to his stage persona and how he constructs routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage persona and performative identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Cook says his onstage persona is a combination of the personalities of his mother, Donna, and his father, George.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article elaborates that this persona lets him be a storyteller, jokey, corny, and vulgar; he describes using exaggerated physicality and vocal delivery drawn from familial influences to 'sell' material. (Includes Cook's own explanation of creating a stage persona that allows wide-ranging comedic approaches.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of online/personal web presence to build audience
rubrics_metrics.description: He is one of the first comedians to use a personal webpage and Myspace to build a large fan base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a career strategy/metric for early-2000s audience building; cited as part of why he grew a large, alarmingly popular following by 2006.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial success — album chart performance and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Retaliation became the highest-charting comedy album in 28 years and went platinum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists multiple albums and their peak chart positions and certifications (e.g., platinum, double platinum), using Billboard/industry chart rankings and RIAA certification as measures of commercial success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arena-level ticket-sales / selling out major venues
rubrics_metrics.description: He was the second comedian to sell out Madison Square Garden's large arena space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selling out major arenas (Madison Square Garden) is cited as an indicator of mass-market popularity and career milestone; contextual details include two sold-out shows in one night and filming for DVD release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media specials and distribution (HBO, Comedy Central, DVD)
rubrics_metrics.description: He performed an HBO special (Vicious Circle), a straight-to-DVD special (Rough Around The Edges), and a Comedy Central special (Isolated Incident).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence on premium TV specials and DVD releases is treated as a career credential and distribution metric that increases visibility and validates standing in the comedy industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance endurance as a publicity/achievement metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Cook broke the Laugh Factory's endurance record by performing on stage for three hours and 50 minutes, later breaking his own record by performing seven hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endurance records are presented as notable achievements and publicity events; the article also notes subsequent record-setting by other comics (Dave Chappelle) for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience attraction — youthful, high-energy appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: One reviewer noted that Cook attracted a young, growing audience through colorful observations and high-energy performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an evaluative comment on the nature of his fanbase and the energy/style that draws them; implies that demographic reach and performance energy are criteria for popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception — perceived (un)funny/industry dislike
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentators in a variety of media sources have characterized Dane Cook's humor as unfunny; peers have criticized him for lack of real material and an inflated ego.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites specific critics and comics (Ron White, Nick DiPaolo, Toucher and Rich radio tournament results, Michigan Daily) demonstrating that peer and critic assessments of originality, material quality, and persona factor into professional reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / accusations of plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: There was widespread Internet discussion regarding three bits from Cook's 2005 album Retaliation and similar bits from Louis C.K.'s 2001 album Live in Houston; Joe Rogan also claimed Cook performed a bit Rogan had developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of joke-similarity or plagiarism are presented as a major evaluative issue for comedians; the article records both accusations and later conciliatory comments (e.g., Louis C.K. suggesting sloppy unconscious borrowing rather than malice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity and timing of material (controversy management)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2012, Cook caused a minor controversy when a joke he made in a comedy club about the 2012 Aurora, Colorado shooting was recorded and made the headlines; he later apologized on Twitter, calling it a 'bad judgment call'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This episode is presented as an example of how topical insensitivity can provoke public backlash and that responses/apologies form part of reputational management; timing and subject-matter sensitivity are thus evaluative criteria for comedians' choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-medium career metrics — film roles and box office performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cook starred in films (Employee of the Month, Good Luck Chuck, My Best Friend's Girl) with varied box office returns (e.g., Employee of the Month: modest $30 million on $12 million budget).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition to film and performance in other media, with box office and critical reception, are used as broader measures of a comedian's commercial viability and mainstream crossover success.
